# 08-fresco — sources

Back-test entry `08-fresco.yaml`: Fresco, the AI scribe for construction superintendents (YC Fall 2024).
Written 2026-10-22 from public material only. Quotes are verbatim from the page named; "Author's choice" marks the
smallest plausible choice made where the public material is silent.

Main sources:
- [HN] Launch HN: Fresco (YC F24), 2024-11-21 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42204939
- [LYC] Launch YC: Fresco, the scribe for construction, 2024-10-23 — https://www.ycombinator.com/launches/M73-fresco-the-scribe-for-construction
- [YCP] YC company page — https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/fresco (now "AI-powered takeoff and estimating for Division 8 construction")
- [KOE] A contractor's daily-log expectations on Procore's support site — https://support.procore.com/tc/Koester/Site_Map/Koester_Expectations_-_Daily_Logs
- [SWI] Swiftask, Procore daily reports page (vendor) — https://swiftask.ai/ai-integration/procore/intelligent-daily-reports
- [BLS] BLS Occupational Outlook, construction managers — https://www.bls.gov/ooh/management/construction-managers.htm
- [OPU] Launch HN: Opusense (field reports for site inspectors), 2025-05-20 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44042791

## The eight founder-emulation items

1. **Who.** Construction superintendents on commercial jobs.
   [HN] "Superintendents are the busiest and most expensive people on construction sites."
   [LYC] "That’s the reality for 210k+ construction superintendents (or supervisors, foremen, PMs, etc.) across the USA."
   → `roles[superintendent]`, `context.actor`, `actor_plural`. Author's choice: "on commercial jobs" (the founders ask
   for introductions to commercial general contractors in [LYC]).

2. **What (the job).** Keep the record of the day's work, for liability and disputes.
   [HN] "30-200 photos per day to document site progress (mostly for liability reasons, or in case of a dispute with the
   owner over delays and deliverables)"; photos used to create "daily logs", "structured documents that account for the
   work done on site on any given day". [KOE] the log is "a critical piece of documentation in the arbitration of a
   dispute". → `statements.problem`, `context.job`, `interpretations.problem`.

3. **When / where.** At the end of the day, after the site walks, in the trailer.
   [HN] "At the end of the day, they'll spend a few hours uploading those photos into OneDrive, or project management
   software like Procore or ACC." [YCP] "We were curious what superintendents were doing for hours in their trailers at
   the end of the day." [LYC] "supes are spending up to 3 hours a day creating documents". → `context.circumstance`, `occasion: daily log`.
   Author's choice: the recall window {5, WORKING_DAYS} and Frequency 4 to 5 working days out of 5 (the posts say "per
   day"; a five-day site week is assumed). Prevalence `p_80_100` ("Nearly all") follows from the same "per day".

4. **Which people (the comparable group).** Superintendents at US general contractors whose jobs run on Procore or ACC.
   [LYC] "210k+ construction superintendents ... across the USA"; "Project management tools like Procore and ACC have
   dramatically increased documentation requirements". [YCP] "driving to Napa, South Bay, and around SF". → `context.segment`,
   `market: US`.

5. **Who pays.** The general contractor, per site.
   [HN] "we charge per site per month, which includes unlimited users on any given construction project".
   → `persona.decision_maker: {role: contractor}`, the BUYER role. Author's choice: the decider is the contractor's
   "operations lead" and the role to test is "The CFO" (a second role, "The project executive", listed); Purchase
   friction's three steps ("A trial on one live job" tested, a Procore check, a security review) and Commitment's step
   "start a paid pilot on one site" are the author's. Public material names no buyer title; [LYC] asks for
   introductions to general contractors by firm, not by role.

6. **Mechanism.** Narrated short videos turned into notes, texted to the crew, pushed to Procore/ACC.
   [HN] "Supers simply take short videos with voiceover, or upload photos, and Fresco does the rest, creating notes with
   transcription, photos, assignees, and due dates. Supers can easily text their crew action items, and receive texts
   back". "We also route this to whatever project management software they're using with a single click."
   [LYC] the narrated example "The beam in the southwest corner of room 134 is corroded and needs replacement by Alex.";
   "Supes who use Fresco complete their notes, on average, 90% faster."
   → `statements.solution`, `solution_mechanism`, Compatibility and Adoption friction items. Relative advantage's two
   benefits are from [HN] ("during their site walks, not after") and [LYC] ("90% faster"); their wording is the author's.

7. **Price.** About $1k per site per month, less with multi-site or multi-month terms.
   [HN] "The typical price is $1k/month, but we offer discounts for multi-month or multi-site commitments."
   → `commercial.price` {800, 1000, month}. Author's choice: the low end of $800 stands for the stated discounts.
   Existing sacrifice: 30 to 60 hours a month per site at an hourly rate of 55 — from [LYC] "up to 3 hours a day" and
   [HN] "a few hours uploading", taken as 1.5 to 3 hours on about twenty working days (author's arithmetic). The rate is
   [BLS] "$55.28 per hour" (median, construction managers, May 2025), the author's stand-in: no superintendent wage is
   in the public material. Ability to pay is derived by code (24% to 61%).

8. **Occasions.** The narrated beam; a school refit report; the uploads and logs at the end of the day.
   [LYC] on a school refit walkthrough: "Normally, creating the final report takes 2+ hours."
   [HN] "few supers have time to do this thoroughly, so these photos aren't very searchable." No named customer quote
   exists in public; the occasions below are scripted from these and from practitioner comments.

## Open
- The verdict was scripted to be plausible and not obviously "build": the problem holds on how often but people
  disagree on whether the log is one of their two worst difficulties; the solution splits on the benefit and on
  talking over videos on site; the price fails (two of eight at the founder's band or above) while the cost it would
  replace is above the price. This is the author's reading of the thread's sceptics, not a measured result.
- No public account names a buyer title at a general contractor; the decider, the tested role "The CFO", the purchase
  steps and the Commitment step are the author's.
- hourly_rate 55 is a proxy (construction managers, not superintendents).
- Existing sacrifice picks use `period: quarter` (the corpus's convention), although the registry's recall period for a
  monthly cost reads "last month"; the values are the monthly figures times three.
- The window {5, WORKING_DAYS} is the author's; the public posts say "per day".

founder.order_why: Most of it runs naturally from context to problem to solution to launch, but 'How should construction superintendents answer?' and 'Who gets a link?' sit under INTERVIEWS · SENT, which reads as choosing the recipients after the study has already gone out.
founder.asked_twice: Screens 3 and 5 carry the same kicker and the same question ('Before we test anything, let's define exactly where this idea applies.'), with the recall-window screen 4 between them.
founder.missing: Nothing asks about the money side: who pays (the general contractor, per site, not the superintendent), the buyer's role (operations lead, with the CFO or project executive signing off), or the price (about $1k per site per month, less for multi-site or multi-month terms). Those are needed to test what the cost it replaces is worth against the price, and to reach contractor buyers rather than only supers. Also missing: the commitment step to ask a buyer for (a paid pilot on one site); 'Offer a pilot?' does not say paid or per site.

PRIMARY.order_why: Screen 4 asks whether I could talk over the site noise before screen 6 has asked whether I'd take videos and narrate on my walks at all, and screen 4's question reads garbled.
PRIMARY.missing: How long the log takes me after the walks, the hours spent uploading photos into Procore, and whether I've had to use the log in a delay dispute with the owner. That record is the reason accuracy matters.

screens.instead: Rows: 'Hours back at the end of the day' · 'Notes done on the site walk, not after' — belief: For most, with it, their last daily log would have given them hours back at the end of the day and notes done on the site walk, not after.

screens.why1: After saying how it fits what supers do now and what it does better, asking what they will have to do to start using it is the obvious next question about my scribe.
screens.why2: The question and hint are plain English to me: setup, extra steps, learning, up to four, nine words each.
screens.why3: I know exactly what a super has to change: narrate short videos on the site walk instead of shooting silent photos, then check the notes before they go to the crew and Procore.
screens.why4: The box took my two steps as I typed them, and the one chip, leaving the dimension out, is the right escape for a founder who isn't sure.
screens.why5: The belief keeps my first step but shortens my 'site walks' to 'walks'; any super reads that as the site walk, but it is a little looser than what I typed.
screens.why7: Both rows are efforts the super takes themselves, a new habit of use and a review step, each at most 9 words in their own voice, with no other role's sign-off and nothing that belongs to Compatibility or Purchase friction; the belief is a 'Most would' built on my first row, and the escape leaves the dimension out as the card requires.
screens.instead: What will they have to do to start using it? (Belief: Most would take short videos and talk over them on site walks.)

screens.why1: Right after I said what supes will have to do to start, Keel shows back the steps it drew from my answer, which is the obvious next screen before I pick one to test.
screens.why2: Short videos you talk over on walks, and checking and fixing the notes before they go out, are how any super would say it; the only wobble is the intro repeating the title word for word.
screens.why3: Both are things the super does with their own hands on their own site walks and log, so they know at once whether they'd do them.
screens.why4: Two distinct single efforts, each under 9 words in a super's words, with no overlap between them and no row missing that my material would add.
screens.why5: The first row is my 'short videos with voiceover' on the walks, and the second is the honest new habit behind my notes going to the crew and to Procore; nothing I typed is twisted.
screens.why7: Each row is one effort the super takes themselves, in base form with no *your*, not Compatibility's Procore fit or Purchase friction's sign-off, and the belief on narrating videos on walks can go either way.

screens.why1: Right after I listed what my supers would have to do to start, Keel asks which one is most likely to stop them, which is the obvious next step before the stranger's question.
screens.why2: Short videos you talk over on the walk, and checking the notes before they go out to the crew or Procore, are how a super would say it.
screens.why3: Both are things a super does on their own on walks and in the trailer, so I can judge which one would stop them.
screens.why4: The two are my own rows, distinct (one at capture on the walk, one at review after), with nothing odd or missing for this pick.
screens.why5: Both rows are word for word what I wrote, and the belief keeps my narrated-video step as I meant it.
screens.why7: Each row is one effort the super takes themselves in their voice, neither repeats Compatibility or Purchase friction, my pick sits first, and the belief can be held or failed against the 1-in-3 bar.

screens.why1: Just before the study goes out, it makes sense to decide whether to collect emails from supers who want to try Fresco on a live job; that is exactly the early sites I'm after.
screens.why2: "Offer a pilot?" and the quoted line respondents will see are plain on first read, and pilots are how GCs and I talk about trying software on one job.
screens.why3: Whether I want leads from the study is my own call, and I know I do.
screens.why4: Yes or no covers it, the two options are distinct, and no escape is needed for a founder's own setting.
screens.why5: My pilot is paid and per site, with the contractor deciding, but "Would you try this for real? Leave your email." reads as a free individual trial, so it drifts slightly from my commercial terms; nothing of mine leaks to respondents.

screens.why1: Picking the interviewer's voice right before the study goes out to supers is an obvious last setup step after the pilot offer.
screens.why2: The question is plain, but the hint packs a lot into one paragraph (video, typing or tapping, credits, recording once, text link), so I would read it twice to see that the 400 credits are the same whichever voice I pick.
screens.why3: I know my supers, guys in trailers and on site walks with their phones, and I can judge which voice they would sit through.
screens.why4: Two named voices with a 5-second preview each are distinct and complete for this choice, and a voice picker needs no escape chip.
screens.why5: Nothing of my product leaks and the actor is kept, but the question says 'your questions' while the hint talks about a voice and my recorded pick says 'the face Keel preselects', so it is unclear whether I am choosing a voice or a face on video.
screens.instead: Which interviewer should ask construction superintendents your questions on video? (Daphne, preselected ▶ Hear · 5 s / Saskia ▶ Hear · 5 s); same 400 credits either way.

screens.why1: After choosing who asks the questions, deciding how supers will answer is the obvious next step before sending the interview out.
screens.why2: Read and tap, an AI on video, or let them pick are plain to me and to a super who lives on a phone in the trailer.
screens.why3: I know my supers: they answer texts and tap through Procore on their phones, so I can judge which format they would actually finish.
screens.why4: The three options are distinct and complete (video AI, text, or both), and none is odd; no escape is needed for a founder's format pick.
screens.why5: Nothing of Fresco's product or the contractor buyer leaks, and the screen keeps my audience as construction superintendents.

screens.why1: Right after choosing how superintendents answer, deciding who gets the link is the obvious next step before sending.
screens.why2: The three options are plain and short; I know at once which fits me, though "Contacts page" assumes I know Keel's layout.
screens.why3: I know who I can reach, the supers I've met driving round Napa and the South Bay, so this is my own call.
screens.why4: The three ways are distinct and cover how I'd reach people: named contacts, a Keel search, or one open link posted where supers gather; no escape is needed for a founder's own choice.
screens.why5: My pick, people I know by name, is kept as typed, and nothing about Fresco leaks into the link choice.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits right beside its deciding number, '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', on every card and in the tally.
screens.why_b2: With no chart here, the kicker and cards still make plain that 4 of the 7 who answered were counted against a bar of 5, so I see at once I'm one short on each belief.
screens.why_b3: All three dimension names and belief lines are word for word the ones I checked on the way in.
screens.why_b4: '5 needed to call it' implies I need one more counted answer per belief, but the screen never says so, never says why 3 of the 7 weren't counted, and never says what this means for my solution.
screens.why_b5: Nothing is claimed beyond the 7 who answered, n stays visible throughout, and the low count is stated plainly rather than read as a lean either way, though the statement under the title repeats itself ('notes with photos, assignees and due dates' twice).
screens.instead: Too few to call on all three: 4 of 7 counted (3 not counted because …), 5 needed, so get at least one more superintendent counted before reading anything into the solution, and fix the doubled 'notes with photos, assignees and due dates' in the statement.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits right beside its deciding number, '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', and the So line repeats both.
screens.why_b2: The bars plainly count 3 for and 1 against over 5 answered, but 'your bar · 4 of 5' with the marker at 4, next to '4 counted', took me a second look to see that it means 4 of 5 must be for, not 4 people counted.
screens.why_b3: The card is titled Compatibility and carries my belief word for word: 'Most construction superintendents could talk over the noise on site.'
screens.why_b4: 'Ray's no is the one to ask about' names a person, but the card never says the plain next step (get one more super's answer) or what a 3-for-1 lean means for whether supers will narrate on the walk.
screens.why_b5: The asked line, 'Think of your last daily log. Could talk over the noise on site?', is subjectless and points at the end-of-day log in the trailer rather than the site walk where the talking happens, so I can't be sure what these four actually answered.
screens.instead: Asked: 'On your last site walk, could you have spoken into your phone over the noise?' -- 3 of 4 said yes, 1 more answer needed to call it; ask Ray what drowned him out.

screens.why_b1: "Too few to call" sits right beside "4 counted · 5 needed to call it", so I know there is no verdict yet and exactly why.
screens.why_b2: The bars read fine (3 a lot better, 1 no difference, 1 of 4 against), but the strip's "your bar · 4 of 5" with the marker at 4 reads like a head count, not my 1-in-3 bar, so I had to look twice to see where the bar sits.
screens.why_b3: The name and belief line are exactly what I checked, though the "You said" line under it keeps only "hours back at the end of the day" and drops "action items to the crew the same day".
screens.why_b4: "Nothing is settled here yet" is generic: it doesn't say that 3 of 4 lean my way, all of them "a lot", or that one more counted superintendent would decide it.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible, Luis's guess is set apart with its reason, and "a small group: a lean, not a call" keeps 3 of 4 from being sold as a result.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 3 of 4 counted said Fresco would have made their last daily log a lot better, 1 said no difference; one more counted superintendent decides it, so send it to one more. You said hours back at the end of the day and action items to the crew the same day.

screens.why_b1: The status *Too few to call* sits right beside *4 counted · 5 needed to call it*, so I know nothing is decided and exactly why.
screens.why_b2: The bars and the five names are plain, but the strip's *your bar · 4 of 5* with its marker at 4 mixes the floor of five people with the one-in-three bar, and I had to look twice to see that 4 is the count, not the bar.
screens.why_b3: *Adoption friction* and *Most would take short videos and talk over them on walks* are the words I checked, and the question asked my supers the same thing.
screens.why_b4: *Nothing is settled here yet* is generic: it doesn't say that one more counted super would make the call, or that two of my three yeses hang on site noise not drowning out their voice.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible and the count line calls it *a small group: a lean, not a call*, with Luis's guess left out by name, so nothing claims more than four people can carry.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 4 counted, 5 needed. 3 of 4 would do it, but 2 only if site noise doesn't drown out their voice, so one more answer settles it, and the noise is the catch to test.

screens.why_b1: Each box opens on "Too few to call" with "4 counted · 5 needed to call it" right under it, so I know both the verdict and the number behind it.
screens.why_b3: Compatibility and Relative advantage carry the belief lines word for word as I checked them, though Adoption friction, which I also checked, has no box here at all.
screens.why_b4: Nothing on the screen says what to do next: not to get one more superintendent's answer to reach five, and not what the two no's mean for the scribe.
screens.why_b5: The counts stay visible, the low n is named as too few to call, and one person's answer is shown as one, with no claim beyond it.
screens.why_b6: Both quotes tell me something I did not write: Ray lets the log slide to morning when subs and the crane slip, and Denise's log is already done on a tablet at the gate while scheduling and subs eat her day, which suggests my pain may sit in the schedule, not the log.
screens.instead: Too few to call: one more superintendent's answer decides it; meanwhile the two who said no both point to schedule and subs, not the log, as what eats the day, so ask that next (and show Adoption friction's box too).

screens.why1: As the first screen it rightly checks that my jobs keep the daily log in software at all before asking about my day.
screens.why2: I'd answer it straight off, but I'd never say 'construction project management software'; on site we just say Procore or ACC, so the long generic phrase takes a second to land.
screens.why3: I know exactly where my jobs' daily logs live, so I can answer it for sure.
screens.why4: Yes or No covers it, nothing overlaps, and a gate has no escape, which is right.
screens.why5: It keeps the founder's segment of jobs run on that kind of software, and nothing about their product or their words for me comes through.
screens.why6: The question says fine once, but 'I'll read 2 options. Yes; or No.' is clunky for a yes-no gate, and §17 says a screener should end with just 'Yes or no.'
screens.instead: Do any of the jobs you run keep their daily log in Procore, ACC or software like it? Yes or no.

screens.why1: Right after asking whether my jobs keep the daily log in Procore-type software, asking if I typed mine up after the walks this week is the obvious next step.
screens.why2: Daily log, site walks and type up are how I talk about it; I can answer on first hearing.
screens.why3: I know whether I sat in the trailer this week punching in the log after walking the job; that's my own day.
screens.why4: Yes or No covers it: I either typed it up after the walk or got it done on the walk. The chips belong to the story box after a Yes, not to this question.
screens.why5: It asks about my log and my walks; nothing about anybody's product or plan reaches me.
screens.why6: One short question and 'Yes or no.' is easy to hear once and answer.
screens.why7: It asks about the problem the founder counted, typing the log up after the walks, rather than just keeping a log. A super who logs on the walk can truly say No and one who does it in the trailer says Yes, there is no escape, and this matches the card's good example.

screens.why1: I just told it I type up my daily log after my walks, so showing me a tool for the walk itself is the obvious next thing before asking what I think of it.
screens.why2: Site walk, Procore, ACC, assignees and due dates are all words I use every day, and talking over a short video is plain enough, even if 'scribe' isn't my word.
screens.why3: I walk the site, take photos, and push stuff into Procore, so I can picture this on my own job.
screens.why4: It's a card to read with nothing to pick.
screens.why5: Part 1 was about my daily log, but the card only ever says 'notes' and crew action items and never says it fills the daily log, so it drifts a bit from the record of the day I was asked about.
screens.why6: Short plain sentences, no parentheses or slashes, and ACC says fine to a super, though the last line repeats what the card already said.
screens.instead: Imagine Fresco, an AI scribe for site walks: you talk over short videos as you walk, it writes your daily log with photos and puts it in Procore or ACC in one click, and texts the crew their items; the people building it believe it would get your daily log done from the walk itself.

screens.why1: Asking whether I could talk over the noise makes sense right after the scribe card, but tying it to my last daily log is abrupt, because I write the log in the trailer and the talking happens out on the walk.
screens.why2: "Could talk over the noise on site?" has no "you" and no "have", so I had to read it twice to work out it was asking about me, and it never says who I'm talking to or into what.
screens.why3: I know how loud my site was, but the question is anchored to the log rather than the walk, and it doesn't say talking into a phone, so I'd half guess what it means.
screens.why4: Yes easily, most of the time, only sometimes and no cover how a loud pour or a quiet interior day goes, and I can't tell fits apart.
screens.why5: Fresco's point is narrating into your phone while you film, but "into your phone" got dropped, so what's left reads like shouting to the crew over a saw.
screens.why6: The options say well as a short list, but "Could talk over the noise on site?" sounds broken when heard, as if a word fell out.
screens.why7: It's an ability with the right four in order and the escape, but the occasion is my last daily log instead of the site walk, and the act has lost "spoken into your phone", so it bends the one-whole-act and occasion rule.
screens.instead: On your last site walk, could you have spoken into your phone over the noise? Yes, easily · Yes, most of the time · Only sometimes · No · I can't tell

screens.why1: Right after the idea card and the noise question, asking whether Fresco would have beaten how I did my last daily log is the obvious next thing to ask me.
screens.why2: I'd just say "my last daily log"; "the last daily log when you had to keep an accurate record of the day's work on site" is a mouthful and makes me read it twice, since every daily log is that record.
screens.why3: I typed up a daily log this week after my walks, so I know exactly how long it took and what I missed, and I can judge whether this would have helped.
screens.why4: A lot better, a little better, no difference and worse cover it cleanly, and I can't tell is there for when I haven't seen it work on my site.
screens.why5: Nothing leaks beyond the idea card shown on purpose, and the founder's job is kept; it is only worded stiffly.
screens.why6: The stem runs past 20 words with that long "when you had to keep an accurate record of the day's work on site" clause, though the four options and the escape say fine as a list.
screens.why7: The item uses the card's fixed four in order, with two for and two against so the belief can hold or fail, one measure of better or not and how much, no founder benefit named, and I can't tell apart as the only escape.
screens.instead: Think of your last daily log. Would Fresco have done it better for you, or not? A lot better · A little better · No difference · Worse · I can't tell

screens.why1: Right after the idea card and the 'would it do better' question, asking whether I'd actually shoot and narrate videos on my walks is the obvious next thing to ask.
screens.why2: Short videos and talking over them on my walks is exactly how I'd say it, nothing I'd have to read twice.
screens.why3: I do the walks myself every day and already take photos, so I know whether I'd talk into a phone while I'm out there.
screens.why4: Yes, only if, probably not, no and I can't tell are distinct and complete, and noise drowning me out is the real catch on a pour day or with the saws going.
screens.why5: Nothing leaks past the idea card shown on purpose; the step is in my words and matches the card's narrated site-walk videos.
screens.why6: One short question with four options I can hold; the noise option is the longest but still says fine aloud.
screens.why7: The effort is one I take myself, the four options sit on the one measure in the card's order with two for and two against, the condition is specific to site work rather than true of any step, and I can't tell is the one escape, though the noise catch echoes screen 4's question.
